claims.statement: Capex framework on track per Q1 2024 commentary
Management plans to maintain average export order book through the year and keep CAPEX commitment of INR 1,500 crores over three years on track
CAPEX of INR 173 crores in Q1 CY24 vs INR 118 crores in Q1 CY23; CAPEX-to-sales at 7%; three-year INR 1,500 crore commitment remains
Hosur greenfield plant first hall construction underway; project expected to be completed by end of CY24; production start expected next year
Export order book promising with >10% sequential rebound in Q1 CY24 vs Q4 CY23 across all regions; Europe inventory optimized, Asia Pacific efforts yielding results
EBITDA margin 18.3% in Q1 CY24 vs 17.9% in Q4 CY23 and 19.1% in Q1 CY23; PAT margin 12.3% vs 11.7% in Q4 CY23 and 13% in Q1 CY23
Localization at 77% in Q1 CY24 vs 75% last year; focus on localizing high-specialty components imported from Europe and supplier purchases outside India
E-axle project progressing per committed timelines; phased investments on track; localization actions started; no further details shared
EBITDA sustained near 18% despite >7% average inflation last year due to localization and cost measures
Committed to investments as per capex framework
Exports to remain in 10-15% range of overall mix; no change to INR 1,500 crore capex plan over 3 years announced in 2022
Capex at 8.4% of sales in Q2, down from 9.4% in Q1; INR 1,500 crore 3-year plan on track with incremental sales already visible
New business wins across automotive technologies, aftermarket, and industrial bearings including IC engine, transmission, 2-wheeler, and continuous process industries
EBITDA margin 18.6% in Q2 vs 18.3% in Q1; PAT margin 12.2%; gross margin improvement contributed INR 86 crore
Savli and Hosur expansions driving new recruitments; railway insulation-coated bearing capacity being added; E-axle localization pending volume scale
Capex will slow down in 2025 after realizing most growth and localization spend in 2024
Cumulative capex for 9M CY2024 is INR 536 crores vs INR 410 crores in 9M CY2023
Capex as percentage of sales increased to 8-8.5% range from ~7% last year
Hosur greenfield plant investment approximately INR 300 crores
Hosur greenfield plant on track to start production early next year with clutch components for transmission

Strong new business wins in Automotive Technologies (clutch, dampers, clutch release systems), Vehicle Lifetime Solutions (steering, suspension, timing kits, wipers, lubricants), and Industrial Solutions (2-wheeler, raw material sector sphe
Standalone EBITDA INR 382.8 crores at 18.5% margin in Q3; 9M EBITDA INR 1,106 crores at 18.5% margin
Consolidated EBITDA 17.7% in Q3 and 17.9% for 9M; lower due to KRSV not yet break-even
9M EBITDA margin declined 50 bps YoY; 30 bps from employee cost inflation, 20 bps from one-time incomes last year
Capex for CY25 and CY26 to be 10-20% lower than the 4-year average of INR 500 crore per year, focusing on efficiency
Future capex primarily for machinery to fill existing buildings in Hosur, Savli, Talegaon; building/infra investment of ~INR 300 crore completed

Substantial new business wins in automotive transmission (clutch, hybrid, planetary gear shafts) for realization in CY25-26; wins also in industrial automation, off-road, construction, railways, linear guides
E-axle localization underway with machines being brought in phased manner; awaiting customer product launches for commercial production
Railway capacity build-up for new products on track; approvals received for new products
Management targets double-digit year-on-year revenue growth for the fourth successive quarter.
Capex for Q1 CY25 was INR 82.5 crores, about half of same period last year; full year capex expected slightly above Q1 run rate.
Fifth plant at Shoolagiri to be operational in second half of CY25; major infrastructure spends completed.
Focus shifting to capacity utilization of existing assets after aggressive capex of INR 1,700-1,800 crores over last 3 years.
Export order book viewed cautiously for short term due to geopolitical developments; expect to sustain current performance level.
Standalone EBITDA margin improved to 19.3% in Q1 CY25 from 18.3% in Q4 CY24; consolidated EBITDA 18.3% due to KRSV drag.
KRSV EBITDA still negative; focus on improving efficiency and margins while top line is on plan.
Capex Q2 2025 at 1,002 mn INR, 6M 2025 at 1,827 mn INR vs 3,286 mn INR in 6M 2024
Fifth manufacturing facility inaugurated at Shoolagiri, Tamil Nadu; total land 108,000 sqm, Phase 1 of 16,500 sqm, ramp up expected by Q4 CY25
Parent company announced €500 million investment in India over 5 years until 2030, averaging ~€100 million per year starting 2026
Current year CAPEX plan intact, focusing on capital efficiency after ₹1,700 crores invested in last 3 years; ramp-up from next year
Q2 CY25 CAPEX spend was ₹100 crores vs ₹82 crores in Q1; moderated vs last year but commitments remain
Shoolagiri plant first hall (16,500 sqm) inaugurated in May; land available to expand 3x current size
E-axle production line at Talegaon: Phase-1 operational with end-of-line testing; Phase-2 expansion underway for more localization
Savli plant: 2 halls built for Gen C large-size bearings, wheel bearings, angular contact ball bearings; lines running at ~90% utilization
Export order book secured for current year; visibility depends on geopolitical situation in Europe and Americas for next year
Consolidated EBITDA 18.7% and EBIT 15.1% after Koovers impact (Koovers EBITDA -15%, EBIT -16.8%)
Overall capacity utilization ~85%, all plants above 80%; Savli plant also above 80%
Capex of INR 400 crores expected in current year and similar amount next year; group CEO announced INR 4,500 crores total investment over next five years up to 2030
claims.value: INR 400 crores (current year), INR 4,500 crores (5 years)

E-axle complete production line investment estimated at INR 200 crores; phased localization underway with phase two targeting assembly start by mid next year
India is global hub for cylindrical roller bearings (CRB) including engineering, design, development and manufacturing; significant volumes exported
Localization and backward integration driving EBITDA margin improvement; localization leads to top-line growth and operating margin improvement
Double digit YoY growth momentum continues, aided by Automotive Technologies and intercompany exports
Better operating margins due to volume and fixed cost absorption
Free cash flow generation and capex realization as planned
Focus on prudent financial management and long-term value creation
Management will not provide EBITDA margin guidance due to multiple sectors and products; aims to sustain YTD operating performance
Capex for 2026 will be better than current year; significant pickup expected from 2027 onwards
Savli plant capacity utilization is around 90%, the highest among all plants
Export order book to USA remains solid despite tariff concerns; US exports are ~INR 100 crores annually
EBITDA margin breached 20% for first time at 20.2% in Q3, up from 19.7% previous quarter, driven by gross margin improvement and fixed cost absorption
Q4 2025 capex was 1,166 mn INR
Capex to step up to average of previous 3 years level, over INR 500 crores in 2026
Target to sustain double-digit growth rate on midterm frame
CY25 capex in range of INR 375-400 crores, moderated deliberately to focus on utilization
Capex as percentage of sales continues at about 4% in Q4
All plants running well above 85% capacity utilization in Q4
Plants can absorb better capital utilization through productivity and OEE improvements
Strong business wins across automotive technologies, vehicle lifetime solutions, and bearings & industrial solutions
Significant business wins in ball bearings, needle roller bearings for 2-wheeler sector and spherical, cylindrical, tapered roller bearings for cement and steel sectors
Q4 EBITDA margin 19.1% vs 20.2% in Q3, full year 19.6% vs 18.5% previous year
Profit after tax margin 12.4% in Q4 vs 12% in Q4 last year, full year 12.7% vs 12.1%
Absorbed 0.8% impact from Labour Code regulatory changes in Q4
Capex was 788 mn INR in Q1 2026
Capex framework remains on track
Full-year export growth outlook revised to 10-12% for CY26
Q1 CY26 EBITDA at INR 483 crores, 19.3% margin, up 18.6% YoY but down 4.5% QoQ
Export order book for CY26 shows minimum 10% growth, solid across Europe, China, Southeast Asia, Americas
Capex guidance for CY26 in range of INR 400-500 crores, picking up from last year's rationalization
Localization level reached 80% overall; industrial bearings around 60% with room to grow but never 100%
Phase 2 of e-axle localization underway including supplier development; Shoolagiri greenfield project machines arriving, second hall planned
Strong business wins in automotive transmission, heavy-duty clutches, hydraulic cam phasers; aftermarket portfolio expansion for BS-VI; bearings wins in spherical roller, housing, large TRBs, CRBs
Working capital levels to remain in check
Q2 EBITDA INR 513 cr at 19.1% margin, up 14.3% YoY and 6.3% QoQ; PAT INR 337 cr at 12.6%
Highest value new business wins in industrial space in Q2 across cylindrical roller bearings, DGBBs, spherical rollers, TRBs and tri-plain bearings
CY26 capex guidance INR 400-500 cr; INR 175 cr spent in H1, remaining INR 250-300 cr planned for H2 with INR 120-170 cr in automotive technologies and rest in B&IS
Capacity constraints at Hosur plant prioritizing OEM over VLS; addressing supply chain and local supplier development to feed both OEM and aftermarket demand
Export share cap at ~20% of revenue for natural hedging; aim to sustain 15-20% export growth but cautious due to geopolitical disruptions
Export share expected to stay 15-20% as domestic market grows 14-15%
Shoolagiri greenfield: second hall building underway; production line from Europe arriving for passenger vehicle transmission
Book-to-bill ratio tracked closely; kept above 1 to confirm growth trajectory
Wind: produced 1.6m bearing for 6MW turbines; building Hall 3 at Savli for wind segment expansion
YTD June performance indicates revenue will cross INR 10,000 crores
Capex framework remains on track
Working capital levels to remain in check
Q3 CY26 capex was INR 182 crores, highest quarterly spend; nine-month capex INR 357 crores
Strong pipeline of new business wins across Automotive Technologies, Vehicle Lifetime Solutions, and Bearings & Industrial Solutions securing future revenue growth
Q3 EBITDA margin 18.7% vs 19.1% previous quarter; pressure from input cost increases due to West Asia crisis impacting energy and fuel prices
